Theme

Latin word

valeō

valeō, valēre, valuī, valitum

verb, second conjugation; with an infinitive mostly in poetry and post-Augustan prose · Conjugation on Wiktionary

be strong enough to, have the power to; to have force, to work, to be effective; be well, feel well; be well, be in good health; of a word: mean, have the force of

In this lexicon

  • able

    also used · classical · Hor. C. 1.34.12–13: valet īma summīs mūtāre … deus (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 4.1.10 (Lewis & Short)

  • effective

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.17.1: valēbunt autem semper arma (Lewis & Short)

  • feel

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō; Traupman 98: minus valeō, melius valeō

  • health

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō

  • mean

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.39: hoc verbum quid valeat, nōn vident; Cic. Fin. 2.13: quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat

  • Minus valeō.: I don’t feel well

    classical

  • Melius valeō.: I feel better

    classical

  • Rēctē valeō.: I’m fine

    classical

  • Mediocriter quidem valeō.: so-so

    modern

Examples

  • sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō. valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē.

    If you are well, good; I am well. Please take the greatest care of your health.Cic. Fam. 14.8.1

    In the entry for feel

    if you are well, good; I am well. Please look after your health with the greatest careCic. Fam. 14.8.1
